name: aiaigasa
title: Ai-ai-gasa
text: The love umbrella: the doodle every schoolkid draws, two names under one canopy. Here it is two people, and the canopy is the red thing.

name: akai-ito
title: Akai ito
text: The red string of fate, tied at birth to the little finger of the one you will meet. Two people, one thread, and a bow because nobody said it had to be tidy.

name: koi-pair
title: Two koi
text: Red cap and gold cap, nose to tail, the circle they make is the point. Neither one leads for long.

name: orizuru-pair
title: Two cranes
text: Paper cranes mate for life, or so the folding tradition insists. Beaks touching; the red one is hers, the cream one is his, and the heart is what fell out of the folds.

name: daifuku-pair
title: Two daifuku
text: Mochi with faces. The one on the right is leaning; the one on the left is letting it. The strawberry is the red.

name: kokeshi-pair
title: Two kokeshi
text: The wooden dolls from the hot-spring towns, heads tilted together. One flower between them, red, because that is how the painters do it.

name: tsuki-usagi
title: Moon rabbits
text: Two rabbits on the hill, the full moon behind them. In Japan the rabbit in the moon is pounding mochi; these two have knocked off for the night.

name: onsen-saru
title: Snow monkeys
text: Two macaques in the hot spring, steam going up, one with the towel folded on its head the way the regulars do. The red faces are real; the monkeys are like that.

name: hanabi-futari
title: Fireworks, two of us
text: Summer festival, the yukata, the two heads from behind, the one red burst. The point of the fireworks is who you watch them with.

name: sakura-heart
title: Sakura heart
text: Five petals, each notched once, arranged until they made a heart instead of a flower. It happens if you leave them alone long enough.

name: mizuhiki-heart
title: Mizuhiki heart
text: The red-and-white paper cord tied on a gift envelope, knotted into a heart. The knot that tightens when you pull on it: that one is for weddings.

name: kanpai
title: Kanpai
text: Two sake cups meeting over the bottle, the clink drawn as three lines because sound has to be drawn somehow. The red is the lacquer on her cup.
